priority_8_elisa_access_plan.access_policy: Four gated phases (Isolated Sandbox -> Read-Only Validation -> Staging -> Production). No phase transition without explicit written approval from Olesia. Read access and write/trigger access are SEPARATE approval gates -- approving one does not imply the other.
standing_rules: Elisa's integration code lives in an isolated module (e.g. agents/elisa) with zero imports from existing routes/models until explicitly merged.
No production credentials shared directly; all access uses scoped, time-bound API keys (crm:read only during validation/staging).
Read-only enforcement happens at BOTH the API layer AND the database layer (Postgres role with GRANT SELECT only).
All keys stored in a secrets manager; none appear in code, commits, or Telegram messages.
Telegram used only for status/task/deployment tracking -- never for real tenant data, credentials, or PII.
Every key has a hard expiration date; renewal requires explicit re-approval, not automatic continuation.
Phase 3 (Staging) cannot begin until feat/rls is merged and its 18-test Postgres run passes -- app-level workspace_filter() alone is not sufficient isolation for an AI agent.
Elisa's write/trigger permissions require a separate, additional approval beyond read-only access.
All of Elisa's actions (not just queries) are logged with a clear agent-identity tag for audit purposes.
Upon completion of Stefano's engagement, all keys and repo access tied to Elisa's integration are revoked immediately.
